messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: GPU pool 'g-pool-3' sustained queue growth > 800 requests for 5m. Autoscaler attempted add (3 -> 6) but failed: quota_exceeded. Avg GPU util 96%, kvcache memory +44% over baseline. Paging to #incidents and @oncall-18.

oncall-18: ack. joining bridge now. seeing >1k queued in the internal queue metric (per-pool). tagging eng-runtime and eng-sre.

maria-sre: joining. quick numbers from metrics: 5m P95 latency spiked from 120ms -> 2.1s. error rate (503) rose from 0.3% -> 6.8%. Top affected customers: 4 high-traffic tenants, spike started ~4501232500 (about ~34m ago).

sam-eng: which deploy rolled? I saw rc1 of model v3.7 pushed ~4501228000. Any config changes?

ryan-runtime: yep v3.7-rc1 rolled global at 4501227900. It increased context window default from 8k -> 16k and enabled new kv-prefill path. We instrumented but not full canary on high-traffic models.

jordan-pm: that aligns with customer reports. escalate: is this a kvcache growth (per-key state) or more tokens per request?

ryan-runtime: digging — looks like both. Prefill now keeps larger prefix in KV cache and we saw per-request kv_entries ~+2.7x. Combined with longer contexts, memory pressure caused more cache misses then heavy re-warm which amplified GPU prefill load.

maria-sre: autoscaler tried to create VMs but cloud returned quota_exceeded; tried different AZs, same. vendor-quota limit 10 additional GPUs for this project.

sam-eng: can we throttle v3.7 traffic or divert to v3.6? We should limit new sessions with extended context.

oncall-18: immediate mitigations: 1) set routing weight for v3.7 -> 0.2 (from 1.0) to reduce qps; 2) enable fallback to v3.6 for existing high-traffic tenants; 3) enable emergency rate limiter at edge for anonymous/unpaid tiers. who can flip routing?

ryan-runtime: I can update routing policy. applying now.

deploy-bot: deploy event: route-weight update v3.7 -> 0.2 initiated by ryan-runtime at 4501234580.

support-bot: Note: Created incident page at https://redwood.incidents/4501234567 (internal).

maria-sre: also raised cloud quota request to vendor: case #CV-9981. but not approved yet.

sam-eng: temporary scale-up strategy: can we spin up dedicated reserved hosts from dedicated fleet (reserved) and redirect some traffic there? That avoids cloud quota.

ryan-runtime: we have spare reserved nodes in us-west that are idle ~2 GPUs. ops says we can provision up to 12 GPUs if we convert a pool but requires a config flip and minor downtime for those customers. ops oncall?

maria-sre: ops approved oncall-admin -> will start provisioning reserved pool and map 3 high-traffic tenants. ETA ~12m.

jordan-pm: customer-impact note: we should send an incident status update ASAP: affected customers list, degraded response times, mitigation steps in progress. I'll draft.

oncall-18: rolling mitigation timeline: 1) route-weight reduction (done) 2) edge rate limiter (in progress) 3) reserve pool mapping (in progress) 4) if still poor -> rollback v3.7 -> v3.6 (last resort). assign owners: ryan -> routing + fallback; maria -> cloud quota + reserve pool; sam -> rollback plan; jordan -> comms.

sam-eng: rollback plan ready. to rollback we need to revert model config and restart pools serving v3.7. estimated 4m to complete if needed.

ryan-runtime: fallback routing to v3.6 for specific tenant IDs done for tenant A and B at 4501234662. Observed queue reduction ~18% in g-pool-3 already.

maria-sre: reserve pool mapping in progress. provisioning 6 GPUs from reserved-capacity, mapping traffic for top-3 tenants to reserved pool.

support-bot: Customer-facing blurb (draft): "We're investigating a service degradation affecting some generation requests. Mitigations in progress; some customers may experience increased latency or 503s. We'll provide updates every 15 minutes." Jordan will post.

jordan-pm: posted public update at 4501234700.

oncall-18: monitoring: queue length trending down from 1100 -> 610 after routing and initial reserved mapping. GPU util on g-pool-3 still ~92% but decreasing. kvcache size flattening.

sam-eng: good. next: enable kvcache conservative eviction (LRU aggressive) and lower per-request prefill window to 8k for v3.7 sessions as an additional mitigation — anyone can flip that?

ryan-runtime: I can push feature flag to limit prefill context to 8k for v3.7 sessions now. Doing it.

deploy-bot: feature flag update: v3.7.prefill_limit=8192 applied by ryan-runtime at 4501234760.

maria-sre: excellent — we see immediate drop in KV churn metrics. Queue ~380 now, P95 latency down to 680ms. Error rate down to 1.9%.

oncall-18: cloud quota still pending. if vendor doesn't approve, plan to keep traffic shifted and schedule formal rollback. Please document exact change window.

jordan-pm: owner for postmortem: sam-eng. target: begin draft within 24h, include root cause (rc1 context change + kv-prefill semantics), timeline, mitigation, and action items (quota guardrails, canary by QPS, autoscaler hard limits, emergency routing knobs).

sam-eng: ack. I'll start postmortem outline.

ryan-runtime: follow-up action: add autoscaler fallback path to use reserved-capacity pool controls instead of cloud API when quota errors observed. filing ticket INF-1729.

maria-sre: file created INF-1729 assigned to eng-infra.

oncall-18: final status at 4501234725: incident mitigated, queue reduced, customers routed to fallback where needed. no ongoing customer suppression planned. keep monitoring for 2h. handoff to next oncall @oncall-19 at 4511230000.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Mitigation in place. Next update scheduled at +15m or on significant change. Please add notes to incident page."
